question: A patient comes to the clinic complaining of severe anal pain and bright red blood after passing stool. What test will the doctor likely do first?

options.A: Upper endoscopy
options.B: Barium swallow
options.C: Proctoscopy
options.D: Liver biopsy

explanation: Well done! When symptoms happen right at the end of the digestive tract, a proctoscopy is the quickest and most direct way to see what's going on. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which piece of equipment is primarily used to elicit deep tendon reflexes during a neurological exam?

options.A: Reflex hammer
options.B: Penlight
options.C: Ophthalmoscope
options.D: Tongue depressor

explanation: A reflex hammer is the standard tool used to gently tap tendons and assess spinal reflex arcs. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which brain pathway is mainly responsible for positive symptoms of psychosis, like hearing voices or seeing things?

options.A: Mesocortical pathway
options.B: Mesolimbic pathway
options.C: Tuberoinfundibular pathway
options.D: Nigrostriatal pathway

explanation: When the mesolimbic pathway becomes hyperactive, it drives those 'positive' symptoms like hallucinations. That's why antipsychotics target this specific area! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h2)

question: How fast do the intense symptoms of a sudden gout attack usually peak?

options.A: Gradually across a full year
options.B: Within 12 to 24 hours
options.C: Right after finishing a heavy meal
options.D: Over several weeks to months

explanation: That's right! Gout attacks come on fast and furious, usually hitting their most painful peak within just half a day to a full day. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h4)

question: Why do non-experimental studies often have high ecological validity?

options.A: They use randomized blinding for all clinical procedures.
options.B: They take place inside strictly controlled laboratory rooms.
options.C: They observe people in their normal, everyday environments.
options.D: They completely eliminate all possible human errors.

explanation: Wonderful job! Since people are being watched in their natural settings rather than a strict lab, the findings reflect real life much better! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which breathing condition is most commonly treated with a steam tent?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Croup
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: You got it! Croup causes that classic barking cough, and warm, moist air is one of the best ways to bring relief. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why is a multi-sectoral approach necessary for the rehabilitation of survivors?

options.A: Medical treatment alone cannot address the complex legal, social, and economic needs of survivors
options.B: Hospitals are legally required to manage police investigations directly
options.C: Social workers are prohibited from entering clinical healthcare facilities
options.D: Nurses possess formal training in criminal law and courtroom advocacy

explanation: Survivors need a combination of health care, legal protection, safe housing, and education, requiring collaboration across multiple professions. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h7)

question: What resource problem often leads to unsafe injection practices in underfunded clinics?

options.A: Excessive supplies of single-use packaging
options.B: Severe shortages of sterile needles and syringes
options.C: An excess of trained supervisory personnel
options.D: Too many mandatory safety meetings

explanation: Spot on. When a facility runs out of basic gear, stressed workers are put in tough spots where maintaining safety becomes a struggle. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h6)

question: A patient is lying flat on their back in bed. When a nurse documents a skin wound, what universal reference posture does the nurse use?

options.A: The resting bed posture of the patient
options.B: The comfortable recovery position
options.C: The prone sleeping position
options.D: The standard anatomical position

explanation: You've got this! No matter how the patient is actually lying down, clinical descriptions always map back to the standard anatomical position as a universal baseline so everyone is on the same page. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the main difference between anabolism and catabolism?

options.A: Anabolism produces waste products, while catabolism produces vitamins
options.B: Anabolism occurs in the stomach, while catabolism happens in the liver
options.C: Anabolism deals only with fats, while catabolism processes water
options.D: Anabolism builds up body tissues, while catabolism breaks down molecules for energy

explanation: Well remembered! Think of anabolism as building up (like construction) and catabolism as breaking down (like demolition to release energy). [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h5)

question: A patient asks how to lower their risk of type 2 diabetes. What is the best starting advice a nurse can give?

options.A: Sleep for at least 12 hours every night without exercising
options.B: Eliminate all carbohydrates completely from every meal
options.C: Take a daily low-dose insulin injection to rest the pancreas
options.D: Adopt a diet high in fiber and increase daily physical activity

explanation: Spot on! Eating healthy fiber and staying active directly fights insulin resistance, which is the root cause of type 2 diabetes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of electronic communication in nursing?

options.A: Exchanging health data and care details using digital tools
options.B: Replacing all face-to-face contact between staff and patients
options.C: Eliminating the need for any written patient records
options.D: Speeding up personal social media chats during shift hours

explanation: Electronic communication uses digital devices to quickly share patient and administrative information across healthcare teams. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary way researchers share their completed findings with the professional community?

options.A: Shredding documents to protect hospital secrets
options.B: Publishing articles in peer-reviewed journals
options.C: Telling patients secretly during hospital discharge
options.D: Posting personal opinions on social media apps

explanation: Peer-reviewed journals are the gold standard for distributing verified research to other professionals. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h7)

question: In type 1 diabetes, which part of the body does the immune system mistakenly attack?

options.A: The lining of the small intestine
options.B: Insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas
options.C: The protective sheaths around nerves
options.D: The membranes lining major joints

explanation: Type 1 diabetes is a classic autoimmune condition where the body turns on its own pancreas, destroying the beta cells that make insulin. Brilliant connection to remember! [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h3)

question: What skill helps a leader look past surface drama and find the real root cause of a ward problem?

options.A: Speed reading
options.B: Blind obedience
options.C: Critical thinking
options.D: Public speaking

explanation: Critical thinking is your detective tool. It helps you dig beneath surface complaints to figure out what is actually causing the trouble on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h6)

question: How do teenagers normally show they are trying to be more independent from their parents?

options.A: Refusing to make any decisions on their own
options.B: Questioning family rules and testing personal boundaries
options.C: Completely cutting off all communication with adults
options.D: Seeking total approval for every daily action

explanation: Testing boundaries and questioning authority is a totally normal way teenagers practice thinking for themselves and building autonomy. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the medical term for the hard bumps of urate crystals that form under the skin in long-standing gout?

options.A: Tophi
options.B: Vesicle
options.C: Nodule
options.D: Pannus

explanation: Tophi are those visible lumps of uric acid crystals that can pop up under the skin or around joints when gout isn't well controlled over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why can slouching lead to tummy troubles like heartburn or constipation?

options.A: It compresses the abdominal organs
options.B: It makes the liver swell in size
options.C: It speeds up intestinal transit too much
options.D: It stops the production of stomach acid

explanation: When you slouch, your upper body squeezes your tummy and intestines like a pinched pipe, which makes digestion a bit uncomfortable. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: A patient wakes up abruptly and wants to walk to the bathroom. What should you do first?

options.A: Insist they use a bedpan instead of walking
options.B: Ask a family member to carry the patient
options.C: Help them stand up and walk very quickly
options.D: Have them sit on the bed edge for a moment

explanation: Allowing the patient to sit up slowly helps prevent sudden blood pressure drops that cause dizziness and falls. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h3)

question: A community living in a very dry, semi-arid desert region is most likely to depend on what primary food source?

options.A: Tropical root vegetables
options.B: Deep-sea marine fish
options.C: Livestock and pastoral products
options.D: Paddy rice cultivation

explanation: When dry climates make traditional crop farming difficult, communities naturally rely on raising hardy animals that can survive the harsh weather. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of Primary Health Care compared to tertiary hospital care?

options.A: Community-level prevention and basic health promotion
options.B: Providing exclusive care for wealthy urban citizens
options.C: Advanced surgical procedures and organ transplants
options.D: Managing rare and complicated genetic diseases

explanation: Primary Health Care brings essential, everyday health services and disease prevention directly into local communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of using a syringe driver in clinical practice?

options.A: To flush blocked intravenous lines rapidly with sterile saline
options.B: To deliver a continuous, controlled amount of medication
options.C: To provide intermittent bolus doses every five minutes
options.D: To measure precise hourly urine output in critical care

explanation: A syringe driver is specifically designed to infuse medications slowly and steadily over a set duration. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h1)

question: What metabolic issue is closely linked to high male hormone levels in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Insulin resistance
options.B: Iron deficiency
options.C: Taking too much Vitamin C
options.D: Eating too much salt

explanation: Spot on! When the body shows insulin resistance, insulin levels rise, which triggers the ovaries to pump out extra androgens. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h3)

question: What does patient autonomy mean in the context of home health care?

options.A: The legal obligation of the family to pay for all medical supplies
options.B: The requirement for patients to live completely independently
options.C: The authority of the nurse to override family member requests
options.D: The right of the patient to make their own choices about care

explanation: Autonomy refers to a patient's right to self-determination and making personal decisions regarding their treatment plan. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for growing and branching the milk ducts during early development?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Estrogen acts like the master gardener, helping the milk duct system grow and branch out nicely inside the breast. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h2)

question: Why is petroleum jelly (Vaseline) gauze usually placed on the wound after a circumcision?

options.A: To dissolve any remaining surgical stitches instantly
options.B: To speed up the natural growth of pubic hair follicles
options.C: To prevent the raw surgical site from sticking to the diaper
options.D: To permanently numb the glans penis against clothing

explanation: Vaseline acts as a gentle, non-stick shield. It keeps the tender healing skin from sticking painfully to the baby's diaper. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h7)

question: What specific tool is commonly used to snip skin threads during suture removal?

options.A: Bandage scissors or suture-removal scissors
options.B: Heavy orthopedic wire cutters
options.C: Standard surgical scalpel handle only
options.D: Disposable plastic tweezers

explanation: Specialized scissors or small curved blades are designed with a tiny hook to slide under the tight thread safely without cutting the skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: What do we call poor baby growth that happens when the placenta fails to send enough food and oxygen?

options.A: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Placental abruption syndrome
options.D: Fetal erythroblastosis

explanation: You nailed it! Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) simply means the baby isn't growing to its full expected weight because the placenta isn't quite coping. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a tactical plan in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To break strategic goals down into medium-term steps
options.B: To replace the need for long-term organizational visions
options.C: To punish staff who fail to meet quotas
options.D: To dictate minute-by-minute patient care tasks

explanation: Tactical plans take big organizational goals and turn them into concrete, achievable projects for specific departments over a couple of years. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is it so important to follow a specific journal's instructions before submitting your paper?

options.A: It eliminates any need to report study limitations in the discussion
options.B: It guarantees that the journal will publish the paper without peer review
options.C: It prevents immediate rejection due to formatting or scope mismatches
options.D: It reduces the total word count of the study to under fifty words

explanation: Right! Journals get tons of papers and will often reject them instantly if they don't follow basic formatting and topic guidelines. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h4)

question: What special room feature do you need for a patient on Airborne Precautions?

options.A: Negative pressure airflow
options.B: An attached private sunroom
options.C: Open windows for natural breeze
options.D: Positive pressure ventilation

explanation: A negative pressure room pulls air in instead of blowing it out into the hallway when the door opens, trapping germs inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: How should you think about a patient who comes in with general joint aches and morning stiffness?

options.A: As a routine case of temporary muscle fatigue from hard work
options.B: As a potential entry point into a complex chronic rheumatic condition
options.C: As a clear sign of an acute infectious disease requiring isolation
options.D: As someone suffering from an irreversible nutritional deficiency

explanation: Those early morning stiffness and joint aches are classic clues. They often give us our first hint that a broader inflammatory or joint issue might be developing. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h1)

question: How is adenomyosis different from a normal uterus?

options.A: Endometrial tissue grows inside the muscular myometrium wall
options.B: The inner lining sheds continuously without hormonal triggers
options.C: Benign fibrous tumors develop on the outer serosal surface
options.D: The entire uterus drops below the pelvic floor muscles

explanation: Think of adenomyosis as the inner lining tissue burrowing into the middle muscle layer of the uterus, making the organ swell and feel tender. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h3)

question: A nurse starts feeling emotionally numb and dreads coming to work after losing several patients. What is the best first step for this nurse?

options.A: Talk things over with colleagues or a supervisor in a support session
options.B: Hide the feelings so nobody thinks you are weak
options.C: Ignore the feelings and pick up extra night shifts
options.D: Resign from nursing immediately

explanation: Never bottle it up! Talking with supportive colleagues helps process heavy emotions and protects you against burnout. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of secondary health prevention in clinical practice?

options.A: Detecting diseases early before symptoms appear
options.B: Preventing an illness from ever starting
options.C: Treating advanced stages of chronic disease
options.D: Rehabilitating patients after a major stroke

explanation: You got it! Secondary prevention is all about catching conditions early while treatment is still super effective. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T5#GNS123_U2_T5_h1)

question: A family demands aggressive life support for a dying patient, but the patient's written living will says 'no'. What should you do?

options.A: Follow the family's demands because they pay the hospital bills
options.B: Refuse to care for the patient until the family leaves the unit
options.C: Ignore both documents and let the doctor make a random choice
options.D: Advocate for the patient's written wishes while offering compassionate support to the family

explanation: A clear, written advance directive from a competent patient always comes first. You must advocate for what your patient wanted while gently comforting the grieving family. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the main difference between disinfection and antisepsis?

options.A: Disinfection targets inanimate surfaces, while antisepsis is applied to living tissue
options.B: Disinfection kills bacterial spores, while antisepsis only removes visible dirt
options.C: Disinfection requires heat, while antisepsis relies entirely on cold water washing
options.D: Disinfection is used on living skin, while antisepsis is used on inanimate tables

explanation: It's all about where it goes! Antiseptics are safe for human skin, while disinfectants are meant for hard surfaces like tables and bed rails. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why is sterilization stricter and more powerful than standard disinfection?

options.A: It only applies to items that touch intact human skin
options.B: It can be completed in a few seconds using simple wipes
options.C: It targets and kills bacterial spores as well as vegetative cells
options.D: It is performed using mild soaps and warm running water

explanation: Disinfection kills a lot of germs, but tough bacterial spores can survive it. Sterilization goes the extra mile to destroy those resilient spores completely! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why do heart conditions often lead to dangerous electrical rhythm problems?

options.A: The brain sends extra electricity to the chest on purpose
options.B: Heart valves open and close too softly
options.C: Red blood cells carry too much oxygen to the nodes
options.D: Damaged or scarred heart muscle messes up normal electrical pathways

explanation: Electricity needs a smooth road to travel. When scar tissue or lack of oxygen damages the heart muscle, the electrical signals get blocked or go haywire, causing erratic heartbeats. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h3)

question: What kind of survey question gives people a fixed list of choices to pick from?

options.A: Unstructured item
options.B: Open-ended item
options.C: Closed-ended item
options.D: Narrative item

explanation: Closed-ended items restrict answers to predefined options, which makes counting and analyzing the responses much easier for your research project. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h2)

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the front soft spot) of a newborn?

options.A: Triangular shape
options.B: Square shape
options.C: Circular shape
options.D: Diamond shape

explanation: The front soft spot (anterior fontanelle) is nicely diamond-shaped. This is a classic midwifery detail that helps you tell it apart from the triangular back soft spot! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h2)

question: Why is it important for nurses to know the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)?

options.A: It tells the nurse the minimum daily protein a patient needs
options.B: It measures the total fiber content in local staple foods
options.C: It helps identify the threshold where nutrient supplements become toxic
options.D: It calculates the exact basal metabolic rate of a toddler

explanation: Smart thinking! The UL warns us when vitamins or minerals cross the line from healthy to harmful. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h5)

question: What is the main goal of providing top-notch reproductive health services in a community?

options.A: Higher rates of untreated sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Decreased maternal and neonatal complications
options.C: Increased maternal and neonatal mortality
options.D: Reduced healthcare utilization among young adults

explanation: You got this! Good reproductive health services catch things early and educate mothers, keeping both them and their babies safe from harm. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h1)

question: What substance do the glands in your ear canal secrete to trap dust and bugs?

options.A: Synovial fluid
options.B: Cerumen
options.C: Saliva
options.D: Sweat

explanation: Cerumen is just the medical term for earwax! It acts as a natural shield protecting your delicate ear canal from dirt and bacteria. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h2)

question: How is true sputum different from ordinary saliva?

options.A: Saliva is thick and colored green or yellow due to infection
options.B: Sputum is produced entirely by glands inside the oral cavity
options.C: Saliva contains high amounts of blood and cellular debris
options.D: Sputum comes from deep in the lungs and lower respiratory tract

explanation: Saliva is just mouth fluid, but sputum comes coughing up from the lungs and bronchial tubes, which is what the lab needs to see. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core principles of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Intersectoral collaboration across multiple fields
options.B: Active community participation in health planning
options.C: Exclusive reliance on advanced foreign technology
options.D: Equitable distribution of essential health services

explanation: Correct! PHC focuses on affordable, appropriate local solutions, not expensive or dependent foreign technology. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of using screening tools like the Internet Addiction Test in nursing?

options.A: To diagnose underlying viral infections transmitted through the internet
options.B: To gather objective data on problematic technology use and its impact
options.C: To measure the exact electrical current flowing through the device battery
options.D: To permanently block harmful websites on the patient's mobile phone

explanation: Just like checking vital signs, screening tools help nurses measure how deeply technology is affecting a patient's life so we can offer the right help. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h5)

question: What main heart rhythm is an AED built to fix with an electrical shock?

options.A: Ventricular fibrillation
options.B: Sinus bradycardia
options.C: First-degree heart block
options.D: Atrial flutter

explanation: An AED is designed to step in during life-threatening rhythms like ventricular fibrillation, resetting the heart's electrical system so it can beat normally again. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h1)

question: Which sign indicates that a patient is developing contrast-induced nephropathy days after an IVP?

options.A: A temporary metallic taste in the mouth
options.B: A sudden rash appearing on the chest
options.C: A delayed rise in serum creatinine levels
options.D: A mild episode of dizziness right after standing

explanation: Kidney injury from contrast dye typically shows up as an abnormal elevation in blood creatinine levels within two days of the test. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h7)

question: What should you do if a patient's room is too dark when you are trying to check their skin?

options.A: Ask the patient to turn on all the household television sets.
options.B: Use a portable examination light to properly view the skin.
options.C: Skip the skin inspection until the patient visits the clinic.
options.D: Rely entirely on touch and palpation to detect any skin rashes.

explanation: Correct! Good lighting is a must for spotting subtle rashes, bruises, or color changes that you'd miss in a dark room. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary activity that takes place during the implementation phase of the health planning cycle?

options.A: Choosing which disease is the most important to study next year
options.B: Writing the initial grant proposal to submit to local government authorities
options.C: Conducting the final research report to present at a university seminar
options.D: Carrying out the planned health activities and delivering services

explanation: Implementation is where the actual work happens, turning plans and strategies into direct health services for the population. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: Why do new mothers need scheduled postnatal check-ups?

options.A: It is primarily required to register the baby's birth certificate
options.B: It helps detect early complications and supports maternal recovery
options.C: It guarantees that the mother will not experience postpartum depression
options.D: It replaces the need for childhood immunizations

explanation: Great thinking! These visits let us keep an eye on physical healing, encourage breastfeeding, and catch any sneaky complications early before they become serious. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h1)

question: Which of these is considered an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?

options.A: Bathing and dressing
options.B: Balancing a checkbook
options.C: Shopping for groceries
options.D: Driving a motor vehicle

explanation: You nailed it! ADLs are the basic self-care tasks we do every day—like bathing, dressing, eating, and moving around. Simple and fundamental! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is a major reason eating disorders often start during the teenage years?

options.A: The permanent loss of taste buds during puberty
options.B: Intense body image concerns combined with rapid physical changes
options.C: Excessive physical exercise required by school curriculums
options.D: A complete lack of appetite caused by hormonal stabilization

explanation: You're doing great! Rapid body changes can make teens super self-conscious, sometimes triggering unhealthy eating habits. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why must nurse researchers pay close attention to ethics during explanatory studies?

options.A: Because ethics boards only approve studies written in foreign languages
options.B: Because testing new interventions or manipulating variables can potentially affect patient safety
options.C: Because hospital patients prefer answering long questionnaires over resting
options.D: Because research ethics only apply to doctors and never to nurses

explanation: You nailed it! Whenever we test new methods or change care routines, keeping our patients safe is always the top priority. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h8)

question: Which feature is essential for a central health care waste storage room?

options.A: Carpeted flooring for noise reduction
options.B: Large glass windows for direct sunlight exposure
options.C: Open access for patients and visitors
options.D: Secure locks to prevent unauthorized entry

explanation: Central storage areas must be locked securely to keep unauthorized persons, scavengers, and animals away from hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: What position should a patient be in when receiving oral medications?

options.A: Upright sitting position
options.B: Flat on their back
options.C: Lying on their left side
options.D: Bent over at the waist

explanation: An upright or elevated sitting position uses gravity to help the patient swallow safely and prevents choking. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a primary responsibility of a medical social worker in home health care?

options.A: Connecting families with community financial and social resources
options.B: Administering intravenous medications and checking wound sites
options.C: Performing physical therapy evaluations after joint replacement surgery
options.D: Designing exercise programs to improve leg strength and balance

explanation: Medical social workers help patients navigate social, emotional, and financial hurdles by linking them to helpful community assistance programs. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h5)

question: A nurse manager wants to use experimental research to improve wound care on the surgical ward. What is the best reason to rely on this type of evidence?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never develop an infection
options.B: It requires zero effort from the nursing staff on duty
options.C: It provides solid proof of which dressing heals wounds the fastest
options.D: It takes less time to read than a short textbook chapter

explanation: Solid causal evidence helps the nurse manager select patient care methods that are scientifically proven to work best. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h8)

question: Which of the following is a major risk factor for respiratory complications in the ICU?

options.A: Eating a high-protein hospital diet
options.B: Mechanical ventilation and artificial airways
options.C: Having normal blood pressure readings
options.D: Walking in the hallway twice a day

explanation: Artificial airways and mechanical ventilators bypass normal body defenses, making it much easier for bacteria to cause pneumonia and for lung tissue to collapse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of the tiny hair-like cilia in your airways?

options.A: Absorb oxygen directly from inhaled air
options.B: Produce special chemicals to break down cell walls
options.C: Secrete thick mucus to trap foreign particles
options.D: Sweep trapped dust and germs upward and away from the lungs

explanation: Cilia use gentle, wave-like motions to push mucus and dirt up and out of your breathing tubes, keeping your lungs clean. [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h2)

options.B: Production of specific IgE antibodies against the bacterial wall
options.C: Maturation of naive T-cells into active helper cells
options.D: Formation of a membrane attack complex that lyses the cell

explanation: You got it! The complement system builds a 'membrane attack complex' that drills holes in the germ until it bursts (lyses). [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is a common everyday habit that shows bias against people with physical disabilities?

options.A: Mandatory medical quarantine during routine community gatherings
options.B: Strict government laws requiring daily public registration
options.C: Speaking to an accompanying person instead of addressing the individual directly
options.D: Automatic exemption from paying all forms of local utility taxes

explanation: Spot on! Talking to their friend or family member instead of the patient assumes their disability affects their mind, which is a common bias we need to unlearn. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T11#GNS225_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical sign to check when monitoring a patient with a suspected brain injury?

options.A: Memory and verbal response
options.B: Grip strength and movement
options.C: Vision and visual fields
options.D: Stomach digestion sounds

explanation: Bowel sounds relate to the gastrointestinal system, whereas motor, speech, memory, and vision checks evaluate specific cerebral lobes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h7)

question: A family member shows signs of severe, prolonged distress months after a patient's death, unable to perform basic daily tasks. What condition does this suggest?

options.A: Temporary fatigue from caregiving
options.B: Standard anticipatory mourning
options.C: Complicated or prolonged grief disorder
options.D: Normal adjustment to everyday life

explanation: When grief remains intense and impairs daily functioning long after the loss, it may require specialized counseling support. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h6)

question: What should happen immediately after a patient's blood pressure check flags a high reading at a community health fair?

options.A: Immediate prescription of lifelong high blood pressure medication
options.B: Reassurance that screening tests are always fully accurate
options.C: Referral for formal diagnostic evaluation by a primary provider
options.D: Immediate admission to an intensive care hospital unit

explanation: Remember, a screening just raises a warning flag—it doesn't give a final diagnosis. The patient needs proper medical follow-up to confirm! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h4)

question: Which of these can act as a natural antigen?

options.A: Sodium chloride salt crystals
options.B: Pollen grains from flowers
options.C: Pure distilled drinking water
options.D: Inert plastic medical tubing

explanation: Pollen carries tiny foreign proteins that can trigger our immune system—which is why allergy season makes people sneeze! [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h1)

question: What do we call positive, exciting stress that motivates you to do your best?

options.A: Distress
options.B: Eustress
options.C: Allostasis
options.D: Homeostasis

explanation: Not all stress is bad! Eustress is that healthy, exciting kind of stress—like feeling pumped before a big nursing exam or presentation. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h3)

question: Why is mixing a sedative with alcohol so dangerous?

options.A: Combining them stops the digestive tract from absorbing any nutrients
options.B: The mixture causes an immediate and permanent increase in blood pressure
options.C: Both substances depress the central nervous system and multiply each other's effects
options.D: Alcohol instantly neutralizes the sedative, causing severe toxic shock in the liver

explanation: Both alcohol and sedatives slow down brain function. Combined, they team up to dangerously depress breathing and heart rate. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h5)

question: A new mother complains that her left calf is severely painful, swollen, and warm to the touch. What should you suspect first?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Postpartum blues
options.C: Uterine atony
options.D: Mastitis

explanation: Warmth, swelling, and pain in just one leg are classic textbook signs of a deep vein thrombosis (DVT)—a blood clot that needs immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: Why is detailed nursing documentation of a patient's nutrition care so important?

options.A: It guarantees the hospital gets zero complaints
options.B: It ensures continuity of care and creates a permanent record
options.C: It lets nurses prescribe their own diet orders
options.D: It replaces the need to give verbal shift handovers

explanation: Well done! Good charting keeps every nurse and team member on the same page across different shifts. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h8)

question: How is a transport monitor different from a simple, pocket-sized pulse oximeter?

options.A: It does not require a power source or battery to function
options.B: It tracks multiple vital parameters simultaneously during critical movement
options.C: It can only measure the patient's body temperature
options.D: It is strictly used for outpatient home care without nursing oversight

explanation: While a pocket oximeter usually only checks oxygen levels, a transport monitor is built to track several vital signs at once during busy or critical moves. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why must sexual partners be treated at the same time when someone has a bacterial STI?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory insurance claim covers the cost of the initial diagnostic workup
options.B: To speed up the metabolic clearance of the antibiotic through the kidneys
options.C: To prevent the patient from becoming immediately reinfected after finishing treatment
options.D: To prevent the development of drug-resistant fungal strains in the community

explanation: Treating partners simultaneously stops the back-and-forth 'ping-pong' spread of the infection between couples. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is an example of a capital budget expense in a hospital?

options.A: Buying disposable syringes for the emergency ward
options.B: Purchasing a brand-new CT scanner
options.C: Paying the monthly electricity bill for the pharmacy
options.D: Covering the weekly wages of ward support staff

explanation: Think of capital budgets as the big fund for expensive, long-lasting equipment and heavy machinery like a CT scanner, rather than daily supplies. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h2)

question: You notice a yellow infectious waste bag is overflowing on your treatment trolley. What should you do?

options.A: Leave the bag open until the end of the shift for the cleaning crew
options.B: Tie the bag securely and replace it with a new one without pressing the contents down
options.C: Press the waste down firmly with both hands to make room for more items
options.D: Transfer some of the infectious waste into the general office dustbin

explanation: Never push down on a waste bag with your hands! Hidden needles or sharp bits can easily pierce the bag and give you a severe injury. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h6)

question: What does professional accountability primarily require a nurse to do?

options.A: Avoid asking senior doctors for professional guidance
options.B: Cover up small mistakes to prevent hospital lawsuits
options.C: Take responsibility for their clinical actions and decisions
options.D: Work twenty-four-hour shifts without taking a break

explanation: Accountability simply means owning your choices and accepting the professional results of the care you give. We stand tall by our actions! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: What can a patient usually eat right after a normal, uncomplicated sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Return to their normal diet right away
options.B: Clear broths only for three days
options.C: Nothing by mouth for 24 hours
options.D: High-fat dairy to coat the stomach

explanation: You nailed it! Unless biopsies or other special steps were taken, patients can jump right back into eating normally. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the minimum number of days between periods that defines oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: 35 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 45 days
options.D: 21 days

explanation: You've got this! Oligomenorrhoea simply means menstrual cycles that are unusually spread out, lasting longer than 35 days. Think of it as infrequent periods. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which type of medication is often given to calm down an overactive bladder?

options.A: Anticholinergics
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Anticoagulants
options.D: Diuretics

explanation: Anticholinergic drugs block the nerve signals that tell the bladder muscle to squeeze too often. It helps the bladder relax! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h7)

question: Why is 'mixed feeding' (giving both breast milk and other foods or liquids) so risky for a baby born to an HIV-positive mum?

options.A: It completely stops the mother's breast milk production overnight
options.B: It causes immediate allergic reactions in the newborn stomach
options.C: It damages the gut lining and increases the risk of viral transmission
options.D: It neutralizes the protective effect of infant antiretroviral syrups

explanation: Mixing feeds irritates a baby's tiny, developing gut, creating tiny gaps that make it much easier for the virus in breast milk to enter their bloodstream. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T12#GNS216_U6_T12_h4)

question: What is the wonderful benefit of placing a newborn baby skin-to-skin on the mother's chest right after birth?

options.A: It helps maintain the baby's body temperature and promotes early breastfeeding
options.B: It replaces the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of neonatal jaundice
options.D: It speeds up the delivery of the remaining placenta

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact is magical! It keeps the baby warm, stabilizes their heart rate, and helps them find the breast easily. Nature at its finest! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h5)

question: By about what percentage does total blood volume increase in a normal pregnancy?
explanation: Spot on! Blood volume almost doubles to nourish the baby and protect the mother from normal blood loss during childbirth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h2)

question: Why is establishing a baseline neurological assessment important for a patient?

options.A: It eliminates the need for vital sign monitoring
options.B: It gives a starting point to track future changes in status
options.C: It completely prevents any future neurological complications
options.D: It determines the patient's exact date of hospital discharge

explanation: Having a clear baseline allows the healthcare team to notice early signs of improvement or deterioration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why must an antiseptic skin prep air-dry completely before inserting an IV catheter?

options.A: To allow the chemical time to kill microorganisms effectively
options.B: To ensure the vein stays dilated and easy to see
options.C: To prevent the sticky dressing from sliding off wet skin
options.D: To keep the patient from feeling a burning sensation

explanation: Antiseptics like chlorhexidine require contact time and drying to achieve their full germ-killing effect. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h5)

question: A post-op patient presses a handheld button on their IV machine to release a safe dose of pain meds. What is this device called?

options.A: Enteral feeding pump
options.B: Large Volume Pump
options.C: Insulin ambulatory pump
options.D: Patient-Controlled Analgesia pump

explanation: That's right! A PCA pump lets patients safely manage their own pain within strict limits set by the care team. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h2)

question: A pregnant client shares that she drank a local root mix to prevent pregnancy before realizing she was already conceiving. How should you respond?

options.A: Report the local healer immediately to local law enforcement authorities
options.B: Assess for any adverse side effects and provide supportive prenatal guidance
options.C: Scold the client harshly for ignoring modern hospital medications
options.D: Assume the pregnancy is completely unaffected without asking questions

explanation: Always keep a warm, non-judgmental attitude. Check in on her symptoms to ensure she's safe, and give her loving prenatal support. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h6)

question: In the HEADSS adolescent screening tool, what does the letter 'S' stand for?

options.A: Suicide and Safety
options.B: Social status
options.C: Sleeping habits
options.D: Skeletal strength

explanation: Spot on! The last section of the HEADSS framework focuses on Suicide risks, depression, and overall Safety behaviors. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which of these behaviors counts as psychological or emotional violence under the VAPP Act?

options.A: Constant intimidation and stalking
options.B: Forgetting to buy household groceries
options.C: Accidental physical injury from sports
options.D: Failing a school promotion examination

explanation: Correct! Mental torture, constant threats, intimidation, and stalking are all forms of psychological abuse covered by the law. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h4)

question: Why do nurses document patient care?

options.A: To prove the nurse worked a full shift
options.B: To provide data for hospital billing only
options.C: To replace verbal handovers entirely
options.D: To communicate care among the healthcare team

explanation: Great job! Writing things down ensures doctors, nurses on other shifts, and therapists all know what is happening with your patient. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h1)

question: What step immediately follows the physician writing a prescription in the unit dispensing workflow?

options.A: The pharmacist reviews and verifies the order
options.B: The ward cleaner organizes the medication cart
options.C: The nurse administers the drug immediately
options.D: The patient pays the hospital cashier

explanation: Before any medication is picked or packaged, the pharmacist must check the prescription for safety and correct dosing. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient with a mild viral cold is given three different strong antibiotics. What does this show?

options.A: The ideal use of the National Essential Medicines List
options.B: Irrational prescribing and potential misuse of drugs
options.C: An excellent example of standard clinical protocol
options.D: A necessary step to prevent common tropical diseases

explanation: Antibiotics don't cure viruses! Giving them unnecessarily is a classic example of drug misuse that we want to avoid. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the medical name for a mouth fungal infection that shows creamy white patches?

options.A: Severe gingivitis
options.B: Chronic xerostomia
options.C: Acute periodontitis
options.D: Oral candidiasis

explanation: Candidiasis (often called thrush) happens when the Candida fungus grows out of control, which is common when a patient's immune system is low. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h4)

question: During the final stage of bone healing, what is the main job of osteoclasts?

options.A: Forming the initial blood clot within the broken bone ends
options.B: Producing new collagen fibers to strengthen the soft callus
options.C: Resorbing excess bone tissue to restore the original bone shape
options.D: Laying down a soft cartilage bridge across the fracture gap

explanation: Think of osteoclasts as the body's sculptors. They clear away any extra, messy bone tissue laid down during healing to smooth the bone back to its normal shape. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T4#GNS112_U7_T4_h2)

question: As a nurse, you notice some IV fluid bottles on the ward shelf have changed color and passed their expiry date. What should you do?

options.A: Take the bottles home to use for domestic cleaning purposes
options.B: Hide the expired bottles in a bottom drawer so nobody notices
options.C: Administer them quickly to unsuspecting patients before they worsen
options.D: Report the expired stock immediately according to facility protocol

explanation: Safety first! Reporting expired stock keeps patients safe and ensures losses are recorded properly instead of silently disappearing. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T8#GNS223_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the main job of nitric oxide when a man gets an erection?

options.A: Stimulating the sympathetic nervous system to contract the prostate
options.B: Relaxing smooth muscle to allow blood to fill the corpora cavernosa
options.C: Constricting local arteries to trap blood inside the pelvic cavity
options.D: Destroying excess fibrous tissue within the tunica albuginea

explanation: Nitric oxide acts like a smooth muscle relaxant in the blood vessels, letting blood rush in and fill the chambers (corpora cavernosa) to create firmness. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h2)

question: Why is folic acid given to women before and during early pregnancy?

options.A: To stop excessive bleeding during the third trimester
options.B: To speed up the onset of active labor pains
options.C: To cure maternal high blood pressure permanently
options.D: To prevent neural tube defects in the developing baby

explanation: Correct! Folic acid is a little vitamin with a big job—it protects the baby's brain and spinal cord development in the early weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h3)

question: What is the term for a medical error that is so shocking and preventable it should simply never happen?

options.A: Sentinel event
options.B: Never event
options.C: Near miss
options.D: Adverse event

explanation: Exactly! 'Never events' are catastrophic mistakes—like operating on the wrong body part—that strict safety rules are built to completely wipe out. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is a key nursing check to perform after a patient receives IV contrast dye?

options.A: Measuring hourly urine output to confirm total bladder atrophy
options.B: Monitoring for delayed allergic reactions like rash, itching, or breathing difficulty
options.C: Checking for immediate loss of hair color around the injection site
options.D: Assessing for sudden paralysis in the lower extremities

explanation: Allergic reactions to contrast dye can sometimes pop up hours later. Always keep an eye out for hives, itching, or any trouble breathing. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is one of the biggest perks for a patient joining a disease-specific support group?

options.A: It replaces the need for professional medical consultations
options.B: It reduces feelings of isolation by connecting people with similar challenges
options.C: It completely stops the progression of the degenerative disease
options.D: It provides financial compensation for medical bills

explanation: Support groups remind patients and families that they are never walking this difficult road alone. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h5)

question: What is the main risk of using a needle that is too short for an intramuscular injection?

options.A: The medicine will absorb too fast into the bloodstream
options.B: Medication enters the subcutaneous fat instead of muscle
options.C: The needle will bend or break inside the bone
options.D: Blood will flow backwards into the syringe instantly

explanation: If the needle fails to pierce past the subcutaneous tissue, the drug deposits in the fat, causing irritation and altered absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary function of peristalsis in the oesophagus?

options.A: Absorbing water into the bloodstream
options.B: Moving swallowed food downward
options.C: Secreting strong digestive enzymes
options.D: Filtering bacteria from liquids

explanation: Peristalsis refers to the wave-like muscle contractions that push food along the digestive tract toward the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h1)

question: What dangerous habit is a common form of erratic medication non-compliance?

options.A: Reporting mild nausea directly to the attending nurse
options.B: Consulting a pharmacist before changing a schedule
options.C: Storing prescription drugs in a cool, dry cupboard
options.D: Taking a double dose to makeup for a missed pill

explanation: Patients often try to compensate for a forgotten pill by taking two at the next scheduled time, which risks drug toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the core problem happening inside the body during all types of shock?

options.A: Inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular oxygenation
options.B: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: Sudden elevation in systemic arterial blood pressure
options.D: Excessive accumulation of bicarbonate in the blood

explanation: Shock means the body's tissues aren't getting enough blood flow and oxygen to keep the cells happy. It's an emergency requiring quick action! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h7)

question: What tool should nurses tell parents to use for measuring liquid children's medicines at home?

options.A: A regular dining teaspoon
options.B: An open plastic drinking cup
options.C: A calibrated oral syringe
options.D: A standard kitchen soup spoon

explanation: Kitchen spoons come in all sizes and lead to wrong doses. Oral syringes give exact measurements every single time. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h8)

question: If a pregnant woman suddenly experiences low blood pressure, what is the immediate effect on the placenta?

options.A: Fetal blood vessels inside the villi multiply rapidly
options.B: The umbilical cord grows longer and stretches out
options.C: Blood flow through the intervillous space decreases
options.D: Maternal and fetal blood begin to mix together fully

explanation: Maternal blood needs good pressure to flow into the placenta. When her pressure drops (hypotension), less blood flows through, which can quickly lead to fetal distress. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h3)

question: If clinic data shows a high rate of patients stopping their birth control, how can a nurse use this to help?

options.A: By ignoring the data since statistics do not affect daily bedside nursing
options.B: By stopping all contraceptive distribution until the government intervenes
options.C: By strengthening pre-conception counseling and managing side effects proactively
options.D: By discharging patients who request a change in their birth control method

explanation: People usually stop using birth control because of side effects. If we counsel them well beforehand and manage those side effects early, they are much more likely to stick with it! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T027#GNS226_U6_T027_h8)

question: Which nursing practice is a great example of direct cost containment?

options.A: Refusing to admit patients who lack private health insurance
options.B: Turning off lights in patient rooms when natural sunlight is available
options.C: Avoiding the hoarding of unused sterile supplies in unit cupboards
options.D: Canceling all staff training sessions to save on travel allowances

explanation: Not hoarding supplies stops items from expiring on shelves and reduces waste. Small daily habits make a huge difference! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h4)

question: How does pharmacological action differ from therapeutic use?

options.A: It explains how the drug works in the body rather than what disease it treats
options.B: It tells the nurse how many pills the patient should swallow
options.C: It describes the financial cost of producing the medication
options.D: It is only used by pharmacists and never looked at by nurses

explanation: Pharmacological action focuses on the cellular or body mechanism, while therapeutic use focuses on the target illness. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h2)

question: A clinic has very little money and must choose between buying new office chairs or running a child immunization drive. What should come first?

options.A: Splitting the money evenly so neither project is fully completed
options.B: Returning the funds to the government to avoid making a choice
options.C: The office chairs because administrative comfort improves staff mood
options.D: The child immunization drive because it prevents disease outbreaks

explanation: You nailed it! Protecting kids from deadly diseases brings a huge public health win compared to upgrading office furniture. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the evaluation step in the nursing process?

options.A: To write the initial medical diagnosis for the patient chart
options.B: To perform the physical head-to-toe baseline assessment
options.C: To administer emergency medications during a crisis
options.D: To determine if the patient met the established care goals

explanation: Exactly! Evaluation is where you check the patient's progress to see if your care plan actually worked or needs a tweak. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h8)

question: Why is exogenous insulin therapy required for clients diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Their kidneys rapidly destroy all oral medications before they reach cells
options.B: Their stomach acid inactivates any dietary carbohydrates they consume
options.C: Their liver stores too much glycogen that oral pills cannot break down
options.D: Their pancreas has undergone autoimmune destruction and produces no insulin

explanation: Because Type 1 diabetes involves a total lack of internal insulin production, patients must receive insulin from an outside source to survive. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why should a nurse always measure height and weight accurately instead of just guessing?

options.A: Inaccurate numbers can lead to dangerous errors in medication dosing
options.B: Patients get offended if the nurse guesses their size
options.C: Estimated numbers make the patient chart look untidy
options.D: Hospital management requires exact figures for billing purposes only

explanation: Many strong drugs, especially for children and critically ill patients, depend on exact body measurements so you don't accidentally give too much or too little. Great job learning the safety rules! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h1)

question: What is the difference between functional and anatomical closure of fetal shunts?

options.A: Functional closure requires surgery, while anatomical closure happens naturally
options.B: Functional closure stops blood flow immediately, while anatomical closure takes time to turn into tissue
options.C: Functional closure happens in the liver, while anatomical closure happens only inside the heart
options.D: Functional closure is permanent, while anatomical closure happens temporarily during crying

explanation: Shunts first stop working mechanically (functional), and later tissue grows to seal them permanently (anatomical). [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h5)

question: Why is the nurse considered the ultimate safety net for medication administration?

options.A: Nurses are legally responsible for manufacturing safe pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Nurses have the final authority to change a doctor's prescription
options.C: Nurses diagnose illnesses independently before ordering medications
options.D: Nurses perform the final check before a drug is given to the patient

explanation: As the last healthcare professional to interact with the patient before drug administration, the nurse catches errors made earlier in the prescribing or dispensing process. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h1)

question: A patient says they want to save their leftover antibiotics for next time. What should you tell them?

options.A: Suggest sharing the remaining pills with family members who catch colds
options.B: Confirm that keeping extra drugs handy saves money on clinic visits
options.C: Explain that incomplete or saved doses promote drug resistance and treatment failure
options.D: Advise the patient to store the leftover capsules in a dark refrigerator

explanation: Always gently correct this common myth! Saving or sharing leftover drugs leads to under-dosing, which is a fast track to creating resistant superbugs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h6)

question: What is the main goal of 'pharmacovigilance' in healthcare?

options.A: To speed up the manufacturing process of experimental drugs
options.B: To advertise new pharmaceutical products to doctors and nurses
options.C: To lower the financial cost of purchasing new prescription medicines
options.D: To monitor and report adverse drug effects to improve patient safety

explanation: Pharmacovigilance is just a fancy word for watching out for drug safety. It's all about tracking bad reactions so we can keep patients safe everywhere. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why can't nurses rely on regular surgical masks when caring for patients with airborne diseases?

options.A: Surgical masks trap moisture and destroy bacterial filters
options.B: Pathogens are small enough to pass through regular mask material
options.C: Droplet nuclei can easily bypass loose-fitting surgical masks
options.D: Surgical masks only protect against blood splashes

explanation: You've got this! Regular surgical masks aren't tightly sealed enough around the edges, meaning those sneaky floating droplet nuclei can slip right past them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T96#GNS214_U1_T96_h1)

question: Which brain chemical is the main driver behind the 'reward loop' when we use gadgets?

options.A: Serotonin
options.B: Melatonin
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Acetylcholine

explanation: Dopamine is our feel-good chemical! Every time a notification pops up or we get a like, dopamine rewards our brain, making us want to check our phones again and again. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h3)

question: What does medical confidentiality require of a nurse caring for an HIV-positive patient in Nigeria?

options.A: Keeping the patient's test results private and sharing them only with explicit consent
options.B: Reporting the patient's name to local community leaders immediately
options.C: Posting the diagnosis on the hospital notice board for staff awareness
options.D: Disclosing the status to the patient's employer during routine checks

explanation: Patient confidentiality is a sacred professional duty, ensuring health details are never shared without permission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h8)

question: Why do many patients with psychosis stop taking their antipsychotic drugs at home?

options.A: Pharmacies give out free drugs
options.B: Doctors prefer short-term use only
options.C: Unpleasant side effects
options.D: The medication cures the disease permanently

explanation: Spot on! Dealing with side effects like weight gain or feeling sluggish is tough, and it's the number one reason patients stop their meds. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T3#GNS324_U4_T3_h5)

question: When do primary menstrual cramps usually hurt the most?

options.A: Exactly halfway through the normal menstrual cycle
options.B: During the first twenty-four hours of menstruation
options.C: On the final day when bleeding has nearly stopped
options.D: Two weeks before the menstrual bleeding begins

explanation: Spot on! Prostaglandin levels peak right at the start of your period, which is why the first day is usually the most painful. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h5)

question: What happens when the chemical signals that control normal cell division break down?

options.A: Cells transform into normal bone
options.B: Cells multiply uncontrollably
options.C: Cells stop dividing permanently
options.D: Cells immediately shrink and die

explanation: Spot on! When the body's natural brakes on the cell cycle fail, cells lose their stop signals and keep dividing, leading to abnormal growth. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h1)

question: How does a nurse act as an effective patient advocate regarding diagnostic imaging?

options.A: By insisting that every patient with joint pain gets a daily CT scan.
options.B: By deciding which diagnostic test a patient needs without consulting a doctor.
options.C: By telling patients that CT scans carry zero health risks of any kind.
options.D: By questioning unneeded scans and confirming that radiation safety steps are followed.

explanation: Nurses advocate for patients by verifying clinical justification, preventing unnecessary radiation exposure, and supporting safe imaging practices. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why are regular compliance checks important in a public healthcare facility?

options.A: They allow nurse managers to change national health laws at any time
options.B: They guarantee that the hospital will never face any emergency situations
options.C: They eliminate the need for any staff training or professional meetings
options.D: They help ensure that daily operations follow established laws and safety policies

explanation: Compliance checks act like a health check-up for hospital rules. They make sure everyone is following safety standards designed to protect patients and public resources. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h5)

question: How does following hospital policies correctly affect patient outcomes?

options.A: It stops patients from needing any medications during admission
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never complain about food
options.C: It completely eliminates all diseases from the hospital ward
options.D: It reduces medical errors through consistent and safe practices

explanation: When everyone follows consistent safety checks, treatments are done right every time, which drastically lowers the risk of patient harm. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which heart sign usually appears late in severe, untreated asphyxia?

options.A: Bounding hypertension
options.B: Severe bradycardia
options.C: Rapid atrial flutter
options.D: Normal sinus rhythm

explanation: At first, the heart pumps faster to cope with the stress. But as the lack of oxygen drags on, the heart muscle gets tired and weak, causing the heart rate to drop dangerously low (bradycardia). [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h4)

question: Which feature is typical of a benign tumor?

options.A: It destroys neighboring healthy organs
options.B: It is enclosed by a fibrous capsule
options.C: It looks completely different from normal cells
options.D: It spreads quickly through the bloodstream

explanation: Benign growths typically form a distinct capsule that separates them from surrounding tissue, making them easier to excise. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h2)

question: What must the nurse check or do immediately before pulling back the syringe plunger to create a vacuum?

options.A: Boil the entire plastic syringe in hot water
options.B: Attach a heavy electrical cord to the back handle
options.C: Ensure the vacuum valves or buttons are closed
options.D: Fill the cylinder completely with sterile water

explanation: If the valves are left open while pulling the plunger, air simply enters the syringe from the outside and no vacuum is created. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: Why do some topical medications bypass first-pass liver metabolism?

options.A: They are formulated to only stay in the top layer of skin cells
options.B: They enter the body without travelling through the digestive tract first
options.C: They require liver enzymes to activate their chemical structure
options.D: They are completely destroyed by skin enzymes before absorption

explanation: Because topical drugs are absorbed through the skin or mucous membranes rather than swallowed, they avoid the portal vein system that leads to early liver metabolism. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h1)

question: Where does the front part of the pituitary gland (anterior pituitary) come from during early development?

options.A: The bony depression of the sphenoid bone known as the sella turcica
options.B: Downward growth of neural tissue directly from the hypothalamus
options.C: An outpouching of the embryonic pharynx called Rathke's pouch
options.D: The mesodermal layer surrounding the developing brain structures

explanation: Rathke's pouch is a fascinating little pocket of tissue from the roof of the mouth that pinches off to form the glandular front part of your pituitary. Embryology can look tricky, but breaking it down makes it simple! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is teamwork and understanding between orthodox nurses and traditional healers becoming important in Nigeria?

options.A: The government has ordered traditional healers to take over all nursing duties
options.B: Traditional healers are now legally required to work inside government psychiatric wards
options.C: Many patients consult traditional healers first, so cooperation improves overall care and safety
options.D: Orthodox medicine has proven entirely ineffective for all mental health conditions

explanation: Spot on! Since many of our people visit traditional healers first, bridging that gap helps us keep patients safe and guide them to timely medical care. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h5)

question: What does the abbreviation 'PO' mean on a drug chart?

options.A: By rectum
options.B: By mouth
options.C: Intravenously
options.D: Under the tongue

explanation: Well done! 'PO' stands for 'per os', a Latin phrase meaning by mouth. It's one of the most common routes you'll administer medications. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h3)
